mainTopic: Which mourning rules (overturning the bed, work, washing, shoes, marital relations, offerings) also apply to a מנודה and a מצורע
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining why a mourner overturns his bed: God's image in man was 'overturned' by sin, so the beds are overturned too. It then goes through one mourning rule after another: work, washing, wearing shoes, marital relations and sending קרבנות. For each rule it first gives the source for an אבל, then asks whether a מנודה and a מצורע share the rule. A ברייתא proves that a מנודה may work, but רב יוסף's proofs for the other rules are pushed off, either with 'לא, אשארא' or by אביי. אביי argues that ostracism by Heaven, as in the מדבר, may be different. When asked how he can call it both lighter and more severe, the גמרא explains that he is unsure and uses the doubt in both directions. For a מצורע, a ברייתא proves he is forbidden in marital relations, but this does not prove the same for a מנודה. Several of the מצורע questions end in תיקו. The amud ends as the גמרא begins a proof, from the פסוקים in יחזקאל, about whether a מצורע may send his קרבנות; the proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the mourner's bed is overturned
steps.stepSummary: This finishes the teaching that explains כפיית המטה: God's image in man was 'overturned' by death, so the mourners overturn their beds.
steps.simpleTranslation: God says: I placed the likeness of My image in people, and because of their sins I overturned it. So let their beds be overturned because of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes a teaching, already in progress, that gives the reason a mourner overturns his bed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People are made in God's image. When someone dies because of sin, that image is 'overturned.' The mourners show this by turning their beds upside down. The idea is measure for measure: an overturned image, an overturned bed.

keyTerms.meaning: Image or likeness, here God's image in man
Overturning the bed, a mourning practice

steps.whyThisMatters: Knowing the reason helps us understand the next question: does someone who is not mourning a death, like a מנודה or a מצורע, also overturn his bed?

phrases.english: The likeness of My image I placed in them,
and because of their sins I overturned it.
Let their beds be overturned on account of it.
phrases.notes: Some versions read כָּפוּ ('overturn'), others read יֵהָפְכוּ ('be overturned'). The meaning is the same.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a reason for overturning the bed that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mourners overturn their beds because God's image in the dead person was 'overturned' because of sin.

steps.title: Does an ostracized person or a leper overturn his bed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a מנודה or a מצורע must overturn his bed the way a mourner does. No answer is found, so the question ends in תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the rule for an ostracized person and a leper about overturning the bed? Let the question stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the mourner's rule of overturning the bed also applies to a מנודה and a מצורע, and leaves the question unresolved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מנודה and a מצורע keep some practices that look like mourning. But nobody has died, so the reason about the 'overturned image' may not fit them. The גמרא cannot settle it, so it says תיקו.

keyTerms.meaning: A person placed under a ban (נידוי) by the court
A person with צרעת, a spiritual skin affliction
Let it stand: the question stays unresolved

steps.confusionAlert: תיקו does not mean the answer is 'no.' It means the גמרא could not decide either way.

phrases.english: An ostracized person and a leper,
what is their status regarding overturning the bed?
Let it stand.

steps.triggerLanguage: מנודה ומצורע מה הן בכפיית המטה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the bed-overturning rule just explained to other people who behave like mourners.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a מנודה and a מצורע are required to overturn their beds.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No answer. The question stays unresolved (תיקו).

steps.title: A mourner may not do work
steps.stepSummary: An אבל may not do work. This is learned from the פסוק that compares mourning to a חג.
steps.simpleTranslation: A mourner may not do work, as it says: 'And I will turn your festivals into mourning.' Just as work is forbidden on a festival, so too a mourner may not work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new mourning law, the ban on work, and gives a פסוק as its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links חג and אבל ('your festivals into mourning'). Since work is forbidden on a חג, the גמרא learns that work is also forbidden to a mourner. This sets up the next questions about the מנודה and the מצורע.
steps.whatToRemember: An אבל may not do work. The source is the פסוק 'והפכתי חגיכם לאבל,' which compares mourning to a festival.

phrases.english: A mourner is forbidden to do work,
as it is written: 'And I will turn your festivals into mourning.'
Just as a festival is forbidden in work —
so too a mourner is forbidden in work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the bed-overturning rule to the next mourning law, the ban on work.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אבל may not do work, learned from the comparison of mourning to a חג.

steps.title: May an ostracized person work?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the ban on work also applies to a מנודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the rule for an ostracized person about doing work?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question. It is setting up the proofs that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We now know an אבל may not work. The question is whether a מנודה, who keeps some mourning-like practices, is also barred from working.

phrases.english: An ostracized person, what is the rule regarding doing work?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether the mourner's ban on work, just taught, also applies to a מנודה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a מנודה may do work.

steps.title: רב יוסף tries to prove that a מנודה may not work
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף cites a ברייתא about fast days: work is banned only by day, 'and you find the same with a מנודה and an אבל.' He suggests this covers every rule, including the ban on work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Come and hear. When they said work is forbidden, they meant only by day, but at night it is allowed. And you find the same with an ostracized person and a mourner. Isn't this talking about all the rules?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings a ברייתא to try to show that a מנודה, like an אבל, may not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists rules for a public fast, including no work by day. Then it says 'the same is true for a מנודה and an אבל.' If 'the same' covers every rule on the list, then a מנודה may not work either.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: introduces a proof from a source
Isn't it so that…? (offers a reading of the proof)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: Come and hear:
When they said work is forbidden,
phrases.notes: This ברייתא is about a public fast day called because there was no rain.

phrases.english: they said it only about the daytime,
but at night it is permitted.
And you find the same with an ostracized person and a mourner.
Is it not about all of them?
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means every rule listed for the fast day, including the ban on work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question about the מנודה and work.
steps.raayaObject: That a מנודה may not do work.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that compares the rules of a fast day to a מנודה and an אבל.

steps.title: The comparison covers only the other rules
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: 'the same' in the ברייתא refers to the other rules, not to the ban on work.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is talking about the rest of the rules.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes aside רב יוסף's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's comparison can be read as covering only the other fast-day rules, not work. So it proves nothing about whether a מנודה may work.

phrases.english: No, it refers to the rest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading 'אכולהו' (all of them) that the proof in step 5 depended on.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected. Nothing is decided yet about whether a מנודה may work.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The comparison in the ברייתא may cover only the other rules, not the ban on work.

steps.title: A ברייתא proves that a מנודה may work
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a מנודה may teach and be taught, and may be hired and hire others. The גמרא concludes from this that a מנודה may work.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: An ostracized person may teach and be taught, may be hired and may hire others. Learn from this that he may work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second proof, and this one succeeds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being 'hired' means working for others. If a מנודה may be hired, he must be allowed to work. So the ban on work does not apply to a מנודה.

keyTerms.meaning: He teaches Torah to others and others teach him
He is hired, and others are hired by him
Learn from it: the proof is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: A מנודה may do work, unlike an אבל, who may not.

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: מְנוּדֶּה שׁוֹנֶה וְשׁוֹנִין לוֹ,
phrases.english: Come and hear: An ostracized person teaches and others teach him,
he is hired and others are hired by him.
Learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תא שמע מנודה שונה ושונין לו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new proof after the first one was rejected.
steps.raayaObject: That a מנודה may do work.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא saying a מנודה may be hired and may hire others.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A מנודה is allowed to do work.

steps.title: May a leper work? Unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a מצורע may work, finds no answer, and ends with תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the rule for a leper about doing work? Let the question stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same question about a מצורע and leaves it unresolved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof about the מנודה does not help with the מצורע, who has his own set of rules. No source decides the question, so it stays open.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two unresolved questions (תיקו) here: whether a מנודה or a מצורע overturns his bed, and whether a מצורע may work.

phrases.english: A leper, what is the rule regarding doing work?
Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the case of the מנודה, the גמרא asks the same question about the מצורע.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a מצורע may do work.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No answer. The question stays unresolved (תיקו).

steps.title: A mourner may not wash
steps.stepSummary: An אבל is forbidden to wash. We learn this from the פסוק 'do not anoint yourself with oil,' because washing counts as part of anointing.
steps.simpleTranslation: A mourner is not allowed to wash, as it is written: 'And do not anoint yourself with oil.' Washing is included in anointing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new rule for an אבל: no washing. It gives a פסוק as the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only says a mourner should not anoint herself with oil. The גמרא says washing is included in anointing, so the ban on anointing covers washing too.

phrases.english: A mourner is forbidden to wash,
as it is written: 'And do not anoint yourself with oil,'
and washing is included in anointing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the work topic to a new mourning rule, washing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אבל may not wash, because washing is included in the ban on anointing.

steps.title: Does the washing ban apply to a person in ban?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a מנודה is also forbidden to wash.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the rule for a person in ban regarding washing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the washing ban also applies to a מנודה. This sets up רב יוסף's proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מנודה has to keep some mourning-style rules. The question is whether washing is one of them, just as the גמרא asked earlier about work.

phrases.english: A person in ban, what is the rule about washing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the אבל's washing rule and asks if it extends to a מנודה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a מנודה is forbidden to wash.

steps.title: רב יוסף's proof from the fast-day ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף quotes a ברייתא. On a fast day only washing the whole body is forbidden, while face, hands and feet are allowed, 'and the same is true for a מנודה and an אבל.' He suggests 'the same' covers washing too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Come and hear. When they said washing is forbidden, they meant only the whole body. Washing the face, hands and feet is allowed. And you find the same with a person in ban and a mourner. Doesn't this mean all the rules?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף tries to answer the question from a ברייתא about fast days. It says the same rules apply to a מנודה and an אבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא ends with 'and you find the same with a מנודה and an אבל.' רב יוסף reads 'the same' as covering every rule mentioned, washing included. If so, a מנודה is also forbidden to wash.

keyTerms.meaning: Doesn't it mean all of them?

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: Come and hear:
When they said washing is forbidden
they meant only his whole body,
but his face, hands and feet are allowed,
and you find the same with a person in ban and a mourner.
Doesn't this mean all the rules?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: That a מנודה is forbidden to wash.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The fast-day ברייתא's closing line, 'and you find the same with a מנודה and an אבל.'

steps.title: The proof is pushed off: 'the same' means the other rules
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'the same' in the ברייתא refers to the other rules, not to washing.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it refers to the rest of the rules.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רב יוסף's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The line 'and you find the same' may only point to some of the fast-day rules, not to washing. So the ברייתא does not prove that a מנודה may not wash, and the question stays open. This is the exact same push-off as in step 6.

phrases.english: No, it refers to the rest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the ברייתא for washing.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'And you find the same' does not have to include washing. It may refer only to the other rules.

steps.title: Washing for a מצורע: left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a מצורע may wash, finds no answer, and ends with תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: A מצורע, what is the rule about washing? Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same question about a מצורע and cannot answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מצורע also keeps some mourning-type rules. No source settles washing for him, so the question is left as תיקו, just like the work question in step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand (the question stays unanswered)

steps.whatToRemember: An אבל may not wash. For a מנודה the proof is pushed off, and for a מצורע the question stays as תיקו.

phrases.english: A metzora, what is the rule about washing?
Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the מנודה to the מצורע on the same washing question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a מצורע is forbidden to wash.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: None. It is left as תיקו.

steps.title: A mourner may not wear shoes
steps.stepSummary: An אבל may not wear shoes. ה׳ specially told יחזקאל to put on his shoes, which shows that every other mourner may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: A mourner is not allowed to wear shoes. Since the Merciful One told יחזקאל, 'Put your shoes on your feet,' we learn that everyone else is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new mourning rule, no wearing shoes. It learns it from the special instructions given to יחזקאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יחזקאל was told to act differently from a normal mourner, and one difference was that he should wear shoes. That means a normal mourner does not wear shoes.
steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק tells יחזקאל to put his shoes ON. The rule comes from the opposite: if he needed a special command, regular mourners do not wear shoes.

phrases.english: A mourner is forbidden to wear shoes,
since the Merciful One said to Yechezkel
'And put your shoes on your feet,'
we learn that everyone else is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from washing to a new mourning rule, shoes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אבל may not wear shoes, as we learn from יחזקאל.

steps.title: Does the shoe ban apply to a person in ban?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a מנודה is also forbidden to wear shoes.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the rule for a person in ban regarding wearing shoes?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same question as before, now about shoes. This sets up רב יוסף's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern repeats. Once the rule for an אבל is set, the גמרא checks whether the מנודה shares it.

phrases.english: A person in ban, what is the rule about wearing shoes?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the question about the מנודה to the shoe rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a מנודה is forbidden to wear shoes.

steps.title: רב יוסף's proof from the fast-day ברייתא about shoes
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף quotes the ברייתא again. On a fast day shoes are forbidden only in the city, not on the road: you put them on when leaving and take them off when entering the city. 'And the same is true for a מנודה and an אבל.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Come and hear. When they said wearing shoes is forbidden, they meant only in the city, but on the road it is allowed. How so? When he goes out on the road he puts them on, and when he enters the city he takes them off. And you find the same with a person in ban and a mourner. Doesn't this mean all the rules?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף again uses the fast-day ברייתא. This time he tries to prove that a מנודה may not wear shoes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא explains that the fast-day shoe ban is only inside the city. It then says the same rules apply to a מנודה and an אבל. רב יוסף reads that as covering the shoe ban too.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: Come and hear:
When they said wearing shoes is forbidden
they meant only in the city,
but on the road it is allowed.
How so?
When he goes out on the road, he puts them on;
when he enters the city, he takes them off.
And you find the same with a person in ban and a mourner.
Doesn't this mean all the rules?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That a מנודה is forbidden to wear shoes.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The fast-day ברייתא's line 'and you find the same with a מנודה and an אבל.'

steps.title: The shoe proof is pushed off the same way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא again answers that 'the same' refers to the other rules, not to shoes.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it refers to the rest of the rules.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רב יוסף's proof about shoes, just as it rejected his proof about washing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'And you find the same' may not include the shoe ban, so nothing is proven about a מנודה. The question is left without a proof from this ברייתא.
steps.whatToRemember: An אבל may not wash or wear shoes. Each time רב יוסף tries to extend the rule to a מנודה from the fast-day ברייתא, the proof is pushed off with 'לא, אשארא.'

phrases.english: No, it refers to the rest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the ברייתא for shoes.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'And you find the same' may refer only to the other rules and not to wearing shoes.

steps.title: May a leper wear shoes? Left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a מצורע may wear shoes. No answer is found, so it ends with תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law for a מצורע about wearing shoes? It stays unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: Just as it asked about a מנודה, the גמרא now asks whether a מצורע is forbidden to wear shoes. It finds no proof and ends with תיקו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as step 13, where the question about a מצורע washing was also left open. Shoes are forbidden to an אבל, and the question is whether a מצורע is treated like an אבל on this point. Nothing settles it.

keyTerms.meaning: A person afflicted with צרעת, a skin disease described in the Torah
"Let it stand": the question stays unresolved

phrases.english: A leper, what is the law about wearing shoes?
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the מנודה shoe question, the גמרא asks the same question about a מצורע.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a מצורע is forbidden to wear shoes like an אבל.

steps.title: A mourner may not have marital relations
steps.stepSummary: An אבל is forbidden to have marital relations. This is learned from דוד, who comforted בת שבע and only then came to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: An אבל is forbidden in marital relations, as it says: "And דוד comforted בת שבע his wife, and came to her." This shows that before that it was forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new restriction of an אבל, marital relations, and brings a פסוק to prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After their child died, the פסוק says דוד first comforted בת שבע and then came to her. The order shows that during the mourning before the comforting, relations were forbidden. This sets up the next question about a מנודה.

keyTerms.meaning: "By implication": we learn this from what the text implies

phrases.english: A mourner is forbidden in marital relations,

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיְנַחֵם דָּוִד אֵת בַּת שֶׁבַע אִשְׁתּוֹ
phrases.english: as it is written: "And David comforted Bat Sheva his wife,
and he came to her,"
which implies that at first it was forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, marital relations, following the same pattern used for shoes in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אבל is forbidden to have marital relations, learned from דוד and בת שבע.

steps.title: Is an ostracized person forbidden in marital relations?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a מנודה is also forbidden in marital relations, like an אבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law for a מנודה about marital relations?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the rule just proven for an אבל also applies to a מנודה. This sets up רב יוסף's attempted proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of question asked about shoes in step 15. Now that relations are forbidden to an אבל, we want to know if a מנודה shares that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A person placed under נידוי, ostracized as a punishment

phrases.english: An ostracized person, what is the law about marital relations?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule of step 19 to a מנודה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a מנודה is forbidden to have marital relations.

steps.title: Proof from the Jews in the wilderness
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף brings a ברייתא: all the years in the מדבר, בני ישראל were מנודים, yet they had marital relations. So a מנודה is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Come and hear: all those years that ישראל were in the מדבר they were ostracized, and they had marital relations.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף tries to answer the question with a proof from the time בני ישראל spent in the מדבר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says בני ישראל were ostracized during those years, yet they still had relations. If people under נידוי had relations, it seems a מנודה is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: "Come and hear": introduces a proof from a source
The wilderness where בני ישראל traveled for forty years

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אוֹתָן שָׁנִים שֶׁהָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּמִּדְבָּר
phrases.english: All those years that Israel were in the wilderness
they were ostracized,
and yet they had marital relations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an answer to the question in step 20.
steps.raayaObject: That a מנודה is permitted to have marital relations.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא that בני ישראל were מנודים in the מדבר yet had relations.

steps.title: אביי: being ostracized by Heaven may be lighter
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof: being ostracized by Heaven may be different, because it is lighter than ostracism by a בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But maybe one ostracized by Heaven is different, because it is lighter.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב יוסף's proof by saying the people in the מדבר were a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the מדבר, the ostracism came from Heaven, not from a human court. אביי suggests that kind of נידוי is lighter, so it may permit relations even if a regular מנודה is forbidden. The proof no longer works.

keyTerms.meaning: "But maybe": suggests another way to explain a source
Someone ostracized by Heaven, not by a human court

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But maybe one ostracized by Heaven is different,
because it is lighter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְדִלְמָא מְנוּדֶּה לַשָּׁמַיִם שָׁאנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב יוסף's proof from step 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the מדבר; the question itself stays open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Ostracism by Heaven may be lighter, so permission there does not prove permission for a regular מנודה.

steps.title: But אביי said it was more severe
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised: אביי now says Heavenly ostracism is lighter, but earlier he said it was more severe.
steps.simpleTranslation: Lighter?! But you said it is more severe!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that אביי seems to contradict himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, when רב יוסף brought proofs from this same ברייתא, אביי rejected them by saying ostracism by Heaven is more severe. Now he rejects a proof by saying it is lighter. He cannot seem to hold both.
steps.confusionAlert: Both moves are אביי's rejections of רב יוסף's proofs. The problem is not the law itself but that אביי used opposite reasons in two places.

phrases.english: Lighter?! But you said it is more severe!
phrases.notes: This points back to what אביי said earlier, that being shunned by Heaven is more severe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning אביי used in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that ostracism by Heaven is lighter.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Earlier אביי rejected proofs by calling it more severe; he contradicts himself.

steps.title: אביי is unsure, so he rejects proofs both ways
steps.stepSummary: אביי is unsure whether Heavenly ostracism is lighter or more severe. So whichever way a proof depends on, he rejects it with the other side.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is in doubt about it. When it goes this way he rejects it, and when it goes that way he rejects it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that אביי is not contradicting himself. He simply does not know which is true, so he can use either side to reject a proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A proof from the מדבר only works if Heavenly ostracism is exactly like a regular one. Since אביי is unsure, a proof that assumes it is not more severe can be rejected by saying "maybe it is more severe," and one that assumes it is not lighter can be rejected by saying "maybe it is lighter." The question about a מנודה and marital relations stays unproven.

keyTerms.meaning: He is in doubt about it
"Go this way": if you go in this direction
He pushes it away, he rejects it

steps.whatToRemember: No proof can be brought from the מדבר about a regular מנודה, because we do not know whether being ostracized by Heaven is lighter or more severe. A doubt can be used to reject proofs in both directions.

phrases.english: He is in doubt about it:
go this way, he rejects it,
and go that way, he rejects it.
phrases.notes: Whichever way a proof leans, he answers it with the other possibility.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the position: אביי holds a doubt, not two opposite opinions.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי holds two opposite opinions about Heavenly ostracism.
steps.terutzMaskana: אביי is uncertain, and the uncertainty is enough to reject any proof from the מדבר.

steps.title: Is a leper forbidden in marital relations?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a מצורע is forbidden in תשמיש המטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law for a מצורע regarding marital relations?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question in the same style as the last one. Before it asked about a מנודה; now it asks about a מצורע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know an אבל is forbidden in marital relations. Now the גמרא checks whether a מצורע, who also lives under restrictions, shares this rule. This sets up the proof that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: A person with צרעת, the skin affliction described in the תורה
What is the law? (a standard question opener)

phrases.english: A leper, what is the law regarding marital relations?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel question: after asking about a מנודה, the גמרא now asks the same thing about a מצורע.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a מצורע is forbidden in marital relations like an אבל.

steps.title: A ברייתא proves a leper is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads 'he shall stay outside his tent' as saying a מצורע is like a מנודה and an אבל and is forbidden in marital relations, because 'tent' means wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a ברייתא says the פסוק 'he shall stay outside his tent' teaches that a מצורע is like a מנודה and an אבל, and is forbidden in marital relations. 'His tent' means his wife, as the פסוק says, 'Go tell them, return to your tents.' Learn from this that he is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that answers the question directly: a מצורע is forbidden in marital relations. It then closes with 'שמע מינה', meaning the question is settled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key move is reading 'his tent' as 'his wife.' The proof comes from the פסוק after מתן תורה, where the men were told to 'return to your tents,' meaning back to their wives. So staying 'outside his tent' means staying away from his wife.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear, which introduces a proof
As it is taught in a ברייתא
His tent, read here as 'his wife'
Learn from this, meaning the proof stands

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it is taught:
"And he shall stay outside his tent"
that he should be like one ostracized and like a mourner,
and he is forbidden in marital relations.
And "his tent" means nothing other than his wife,
as it says: "Go say to them,
return to your tents."
phrases.notes: דברים 5:27. After מתן תורה the men were allowed back to their wives.

phrases.english: Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That a מצורע is forbidden in marital relations.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading ויקרא 14:8 together with דברים 5:27.

steps.title: Can this also settle the question about a מנודה?
steps.stepSummary: Since the ברייתא compares a מצורע to a מנודה, the גמרא asks if this proves a מנודה is also forbidden in marital relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can we also settle the question about a מנודה from this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its earlier open question from step 20. It suggests the ברייתא might also prove that a מנודה is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said a מצורע is 'like a מנודה and like an אבל, and forbidden in marital relations.' Read quickly, that sounds like the ban comes from being like a מנודה, which would mean a מנודה is forbidden too. Steps 21-24 had left this question open.

keyTerms.meaning: And let us resolve (settle a question that was left open)

phrases.english: And let us also resolve it for one who is ostracized?
phrases.notes: This is the question from step 20 that אביי kept blocking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא of step 26 to try to settle the open question of step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the ברייתא's comparison of a מצורע to a מנודה proves a מנודה is forbidden in marital relations.

steps.title: The comparison is about other things only
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף, quoted by רב הונא בריה דרב פנחס, explains that the ברייתא compares the מצורע to a מנודה in other matters and then adds the marital ban as a separate rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב פנחס said in the name of רב יוסף: Does it say 'that he is forbidden' like them? It says he is like a מנודה and an אבל in other matters, and he is also forbidden in marital relations.
steps.whatsHappening: The attempt to settle the מנודה question is blocked. The ברייתא's comparison does not cover marital relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists two separate points. First, the מצורע is like a מנודה and an אבל in other restrictions. Second, as an extra rule, he is forbidden in marital relations. So the marital ban is a rule for the מצורע alone and tells us nothing about a מנודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Does it actually say...? (a challenge to how a text is being read)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read the ברייתא as 'he is like a מנודה, so he is forbidden.' The 'and' (וְ) starts a new, separate rule.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב פִּנְחָס
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Pinchas said
in the name of Rav Yosef:
Does it teach 'that he is forbidden'?
phrases.notes: He means: does it say he is forbidden because he is like a מנודה? No.

phrases.english: That he should be like one ostracized and like a mourner
in other matters,
and he is also forbidden in marital relations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of step 27 by rereading the ברייתא's wording.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the attempt to learn the מנודה rule from the ברייתא. The ruling for a מצורע stays.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The step 27 attempt reads the marital ban as part of the comparison to a מנודה, but the ban is a separate, added rule.
steps.whatToRemember: A מצורע is forbidden in marital relations. Whether a מנודה is forbidden is still unresolved.

steps.title: A mourner does not send his offerings
steps.stepSummary: An אבל does not bring his קרבנות, as רבי שמעון learns from the word שלמים: offered when one is שלם, whole, and not while one is an אונן.
steps.simpleTranslation: An אבל does not send his קרבנות, as it is taught: רבי שמעון says, 'שלמים' means when he is whole, not when he is an אונן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new restriction of an אבל: he does not bring קרבנות. It gives the source for this. This sets up the next question about a מנודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון connects the name שלמים to the word שלם, 'whole' or settled. A person in fresh mourning (an אונן) is not settled in mind, so he does not bring these offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: Sends his offerings to the בית המקדש
A mourner in the earliest stage of mourning

phrases.english: A mourner does not send his offerings,
as it is taught: Rabbi Shimon says:
"Shelamim": at a time when he is whole,
and not at a time when he is in acute mourning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic in the list of an אבל's restrictions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אבל (אונן) does not bring his קרבנות, learned from the word שלמים.

steps.title: May an ostracized person send his offerings?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a מנודה, like an אבל, may not bring his קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law: may a מנודה send his קרבנות?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the rule just stated for an אבל also applies to a מנודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as before: take an אבל's restriction and check whether a מנודה shares it. Here the restriction is bringing קרבנות.

phrases.english: One who is ostracized, what is the law: may he send his offerings?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the אבל rule of step 29 to a מנודה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a מנודה may bring his קרבנות.

steps.title: Proof from the generation in the wilderness
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the Jews in the מדבר were מנודים, yet they brought קרבנות, so a מנודה may bring them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Come and hear: all the years the Jews were in the מדבר they were מנודים, and they still sent their קרבנות.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף tries to answer the question with the same source he used in step 21 for marital relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the whole nation was in נידוי and still brought קרבנות, then נידוי does not stop a person from bringing them. This is the same kind of proof as before, now applied to קרבנות.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: Come and hear:
All those years
that the Jews were in the wilderness
they were ostracized,
and they sent their offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attempts to answer step 30 using the source from step 21.
steps.raayaObject: That a מנודה may bring his קרבנות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא saying the Jews in the מדבר were מנודים yet brought קרבנות.

steps.title: אביי: Heavenly ostracism may be lighter
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof: being ostracized by Heaven may be different because it is lighter than a בית דין's ostracism.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Perhaps one ostracized by Heaven is different, because it is lighter.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי blocks רב יוסף's proof, just as he did in step 22.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The generation in the מדבר was placed in נידוי by Heaven, not by a בית דין. If Heavenly נידוי is lighter, the fact that they brought קרבנות does not prove a regular מנודה may. As step 24 explained, אביי is unsure which kind is lighter, so he can use either side to reject a proof.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But perhaps one ostracized by Heaven is different, since it is lighter?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 31.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the מדבר generation only, not the question itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Heavenly נידוי may be lighter than a בית דין's, so the case cannot be applied to a regular מנודה.

steps.title: Did אביי not say Heaven's ostracism is more serious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי for calling Heaven's ostracism lighter, when elsewhere he called it heavier.
steps.simpleTranslation: Lighter?! But you yourself said it is more serious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised by אביי's rejection and points out that he seems to contradict himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 32 אביי said being shunned by Heaven may be lighter than being shunned by a בית דין. But elsewhere אביי said being shunned by Heaven is heavier. So how can he call it lighter here?

phrases.english: Is it lighter?!
But you said it is more serious!
phrases.notes: "You" means אביי. Somewhere else he said that being shunned by Heaven is the heavier one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning אביי used in his rejection in step 32.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that Heaven's ostracism is lighter than a בית דין's.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אביי himself said elsewhere that Heaven's ostracism is heavier, so he contradicts himself.

steps.title: אביי is unsure, so he rejects the proof either way
steps.stepSummary: אביי is in doubt about which ostracism is more serious, so he uses the doubt to reject רב יוסף's proofs in both directions.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is unsure about it, and so he pushes back on him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that אביי never decided which ostracism is heavier. He is in doubt, and he uses that doubt to push back on רב יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A proof only works if the two cases are surely alike. Because אביי is unsure whether Heaven's ostracism is lighter or heavier, he can say 'maybe it is different' to any proof. So 'lighter' here and 'heavier' elsewhere do not contradict each other. Each is just a possibility he raises to block a proof.

keyTerms.meaning: He pushes him off, rejects his argument

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not ruling that Heaven's ostracism is lighter. He is only saying 'maybe', and that is enough to knock down a proof.
steps.whatToRemember: The question from step 30, whether a מנודה may bring קרבנות, is left without a proof. אביי's doubt blocks רב יוסף's proof from the people in the מדבר.

phrases.english: He is uncertain about it
phrases.notes: "He" is אביי. He doesn't know whether Heaven's ostracism is lighter or heavier.

phrases.english: and so he rejects him (in both directions).
phrases.notes: "Him" is רב יוסף. Whatever proof רב יוסף brings, אביי can answer, "maybe it's different."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing: the statement was a doubt, not a firm position
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי held two opposite firm views about Heaven's ostracism.
steps.terutzMaskana: אביי is unsure, so he can raise either side to block a proof.

steps.title: May a leper send his offerings?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a מצורע may send his קרבנות to the בית המקדש to be offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law about a מצורע sending his קרבנות?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. It continues the list of people from earlier (the אבל and the מנודה) and asks the same question about a מצורע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We learned that an אבל does not bring his קרבנות (step 29), and the question about a מנודה was left open (steps 30-34). Now the גמרא asks about a מצורע. The question is whether he, like an אבל, may not send his קרבנות to be offered for him.

keyTerms.meaning: A person with צרעת, a spiritual skin disease

phrases.english: A leper, what is the law about his sending his offerings?
phrases.notes: "Sending" means having his offerings brought to the בית המקדש and offered for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the same question about a מצורע that was asked about the אבל and the מנודה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a מצורע may send his קרבנות to be offered.

steps.title: A proof begins from יחזקאל's verse about a כהן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a proof from a ברייתא that explains the פסוקים in יחזקאל about a כהן who became impure from a dead relative.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as a ברייתא teaches: "And after his purification" means after he separates from the dead person. "They shall count for him seven days" means the seven days of his counting. "And on the day he comes into the holy place, into the inner courtyard, to serve in the holy place, he shall offer his sin-offering"...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts bringing a proof for the מצורע question. This step only sets up the proof by quoting a ברייתא. The part that actually answers the question comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא goes through the פסוקים one phrase at a time. A כהן who became impure from a dead relative first separates from the dead body. Then he counts seven days. Then, on the day he returns to serve, he brings a חטאת. The point that answers our question has not come yet; this is the base text it will rely on.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear, a signal that a proof is coming

steps.confusionAlert: This step is only the setup. The ברייתא is not finished here, and the proof about the מצורע has not been made yet.

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it is taught in a ברייתא:
"And after his purification" means after he separates from the dead,
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 44:26. The פסוק is about a כהן who became impure from a dead relative.

phrases.english: "They shall count for him seven days":
these are the seven days of his counting,
"And on the day he comes into the holy place,
into the inner courtyard,
to serve in the holy place,
he shall offer his sin-offering":

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question from step 35 by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: Whether a מצורע may send his קרבנות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא explaining יחזקאל 44:26-27 about a כהן who became impure from a dead body. The ברייתא continues on the next amud.
